content.title: KITCHEN FIXES THAT WORK FASTER THAN YOUR MEDICINE CABINET
facts: **Hiccups** – Swallow 1 teaspoon of dry sugar; it resets the nerve that's misfiring.
**Burnt Tongue** – Press a spoonful of plain yogurt on it for instant cooling relief.
**Stuffy Nose** – Hold a warm, damp washcloth over your sinuses for 2 minutes to loosen mucus.
**Toothache** – Dab a small amount of clove oil on the sore spot to numb it naturally.
**Bad Breath** – Chew 1 teaspoon of fennel seeds; their oils neutralize odor-causing bacteria.
**Sore Throat** – Gargle warm water with 1/2 teaspoon salt every few hours to pull out swelling.
**Leg Cramp at Night** – Pull your toes toward your shin for 15 seconds to force the muscle to release.
**Stinky Hands After Cooking** – Rub them on stainless steel under running water to neutralize garlic/onion smell.
**Dry, Cracked Lips** – Dab a thin layer of honey on them before bed to lock in moisture overnight.
**Hangnail Pain** – Soak the finger in warm water with 1 tablespoon olive oil for 5 minutes to soften skin.
**Follow along** – for more quick, harmless fixes you can use the same day.
content.caption:
A few of these are oddly satisfying once you know why they work. The dry sugar trick for hiccups isn't a myth — the granules scratch the back of your throat just enough to interrupt the phrenic nerve spasm that's causing the hiccup in the first place. Clove oil for a toothache works because it contains eugenol, a natural compound that numbs nerve endings almost like a mild anesthetic. And that leg cramp stretch — pulling your toes toward your shin — physically forces the calf muscle to lengthen, which overrides the spasm signal your nerves are sending. Everyone's body responds a little differently, so give these a try and see what works for you.
